title: Proactive Capacity Intervention Canvas
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the "Proactive Capacity Intervention Canvas" — a structured decision and runbook artifact for preemptive capacity actions driven by SLO telemetry, predictive signals, and business-priority constraints. The goal is to reduce SLO burn before critical error-budget depletion while minimizing cost and customer impact.

Intended audience
- SREs who operate inference clusters and multi-tenant schedulers
- Oncall owners and incident commanders (ICs) for model-serving services
- Product and platform stakeholders who authorize capacity interventions

When to use this playbook
- Observability predicts a >= 60% probability of crossing a primary SLO (p99 latency or availability) within the next 6 hours.
- Error budget consumption rate (burn rate) is > 2x baseline and trending up.
- Business tier tenants (Enterprise / Dedicated) show anomalous token patterns that would cause downstream SLA breaches.

Key concepts and definitions
- Primary SLOs: service-level objectives that drive customer-facing SLAs (examples: request p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate).
- Predictive signal: model output from the SLO Prognostics pipeline indicating probability and confidence of SLO breach.
- Intervention: any capacity or routing change (scale up, re-route, preemptive eviction, soft-throttle).
- Evidence bundle: a collection of telemetry files and traces attached to the decision for later review (see Evidence section).

Decision canvas (executive summary)
1) Validate signals
   - Confirm SLO telemetry (p99, p95, error rate) and provisioning metrics (GPU utilization, queue depth).
   - Verify predictive score >= 0.6 AND burn-rate > threshold in Table 1.
2) Classify impact
   - Impact tier: Critical (tier A), Important (tier B), Low (tier C) — map against tenant priority and active incidents.
3) Select intervention strategy
   - Prefer non-disruptive actions first (routing, temporary model downgrades, KV cache hot-refresh).
   - Escalate to capacity expansion only if non-disruptive steps don't reduce predictive score by >= 40%.
4) Execute with safety net
   - Run pre-flight checks, snapshot capacity state, and attach evidence bundle marker.
   - Execute (see Runbook).
5) Observe and revert if necessary
   - If SLOs improve and burn-rate reduces, retain change for minimum stabilization window (30–60 minutes).
   - If not, revert and begin mitigation escalation.

Table 1 — Signals, thresholds, and initial actions\n(Use this as a quick reference; thresholds above can be tuned per service)

| Signal | Threshold | Initial action |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Predictive breach probability | >= 0.60 | Run preflight; apply routing spill to secondary region (soft 10%) |
| Error budget burn-rate | > 2.0x | Enable temporary token-priority shaping; notify product owners |
| GPU avg util (5m) | > 75% and queue depth > 100 | Warm additional model pools; trigger scale-up policy |
| Model KV cache miss rate | > 15% | Warm cache by synthetic prefix replay (see tooling) |
| Tail latencies (p99) | > 1.5x baseline | Redirect low-priority requests to quantized model variant |

Runbook: Preemptive capacity interventions (step-by-step)

1) Validate telemetry and prepare evidence bundle
   - CLI: rwi query-slo --service <svc> --window 15m --quantiles p50,p95,p99 --output json > evidence/slo-<svc>-$(date +%s).json
   - Grab recent traces: rwi traces export --service <svc> --since 30m --output evidence/traces-<svc>-$(date +%s).har
   - Attach logs: rwi logs fetch --service <svc> --severity error --since 30m --output evidence/logs-<svc>-$(date +%s).ndjson

2) Preflight checks (automated, run sequentially)\   a) Capacity sanity: rwi capacity check --service <svc> --expected-headroom 20%\   b) Model compatibility: rwi model-compat --model <model-id> --region <r>\   c) Deployment health: kubectl get pods -l app=<svc> -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Running

3) Non-disruptive interventions (try in order; allow 10–15 minutes for signal stabilization each)\   a) Routing spill: rwi route adjust --service <svc> --route spill --percent 10 --to region-secondary\   b) Token-priority shaping: rwi throttle set --service <svc> --policy spike-protection --soft-limit 80%\   c) Model variant downgrade: rwi model activate --service <svc> --variant quantized-v2 --traffic 15%\   d) Cache warm: rwi cache replay --service <svc> --prefixes top-100 --concurrency 4

4) Capacity expansion (if non-disruptive steps insufficient)\   a) Warm scale: rwi capacity reserve --pool inference-hot --gpus 4 --duration 2h --owner oncall\   b) Provisioning: infractl provision-gpu --type a2-highcpu --count 4 --tag proactive-intervention\   c) Orchestration: redwoodctl rollout start --service <svc> --annotation "proactive-scale"

5) Stabilization and retention\   - Minimum stabilization window: 30 minutes after primary SLO returns below alert threshold.
   - Record retention reason and duration in the evidence bundle.

6) Reversion and escalation\   - If intervention increases burn rate or latency, revert the last change immediately using the stored snapshot: rwi revert --snapshot <id>\   - Escalate to IC and open incident per Incident Process: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-review/incident-process

Evidence and post-action review
- Every proactive intervention must create an evidence bundle and a short post-action note in the incident tracker even if it does not become a full incident. The evidence bundle should include:
  - SLO snapshot JSON, traces HAR, logs ndjson, capacity and cluster metrics (CSV), and the intervention command history (shell transcript).
- Attach the evidence bundle with tags: service:<svc>, intervention:proactive, owner:<oncall>
- Within 72 hours, the oncall owner must add a 1–2 paragraph rationale and outcome to the intervention record; reviewers (see metadata) will confirm whether the action was necessary and effective.

Telemetry and tooling integrations
- SLO Prognostics: the predictive pipeline that emits breach probability and confidence. Hook: /api/prognostics/v1/predictions
- Capacity Orchestrator (caporch): accepts reserve and release API calls. Hook examples below.
- Observability: use the rwi CLI (internal wrapper) to fetch consolidated SLO/trace/log bundles.

Example: call to Capacity Orchestrator (caporch)\

POST /v1/reservations
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "service": "inference-embedder",
  "pool": "inference-hot",
  "gpus": 4,
  "duration_minutes": 120,
  "reason": "Proactive capacity intervention — high predictive breach probability"
}

Operationally sensitive knobs and safe limits
- Reserve requests automatically capped at 20 GPUs per cluster per tenant without approval.
- Automated rollouts that touch traffic > 25% must be pre-approved by the platform pager.
- Any eviction/soft-preemption affecting >10% of a tenant's concurrent requests requires product owner signoff via Slack #prod-escrow or PagerDuty webhook.

Ownership and communications
- Primary owner: inference-sre-team (oncall rotation)
- Secondary owner: runtime-ops (capacity orchestration team)
- Product stakeholder: owner listed on the customer-ticket or the tenant contract page
- Communication channels: Slack (dedicated channel), Incident tracker, and customer-facing status page if an SLA is impacted

KPIs and success criteria
- Intervention success = reduction in predictive breach probability by >= 40% within 30 minutes and reduction of burn-rate to <= 1.2x baseline.
- False positive rate (unnecessary interventions) should be < 15% per quarter.
- Average cost-per-intervention tracked and reconciled monthly to identify expensive mitigation patterns.

Postmortem and continuous improvement
- If an intervention becomes an incident (SLO breach despite action), run a targeted postmortem following the Incident Review Standards: include hypothesis reproduction, evidence bundle, and remediation plan.
- Quarterly: SREs and product owners will review intervention inventory, tune predictive thresholds, and update the canvas.

Appendix A — Example evidence bundle manifest (manifest.json)
{
  "service": "inference-embedder",
  "intervention_id": "pi-20250301-0234",
  "predicted_breach_probability": "0.68",
  "actions_taken": ["route-spill-10%","cache-replay","reserve-4-gpus"],
  "artifacts": ["slo.json","traces.har","logs.ndjson","capacity.csv","commands.sh"]
}

Appendix B — Quick checklist for oncall (one-page)
- [ ] Validate predictive signal and current SLOs
- [ ] Run preflight checks (capacity, model compat, deployments)
- [ ] Try non-disruptive measures in order (routing -> shaping -> variant)
- [ ] If needed, reserve capacity with caporch and annotate snapshot ID
- [ ] Wait stabilization window (30–60m), confirm KPI improvements
- [ ] Create evidence bundle and add rationale in tracker (72h)
